summary: Modoc County, CA all-steel 100 ft lookout reported on the Tulelake refuge in 1937; Forest Lookouts marks it removed; no source ties the 1938 towers to it.

facts.design: All-steel lookout tower with a small steel house on top, on steel base beams and concrete foundations
facts.status_note: Forest Lookouts marks the entry Removed, with no date or details

events.note: January 1937 newspaper report, filed under the Peninsula heading: CCC men of Clear Lake camp completed an all-steel lookout tower, 100 feet tall
July 1938 report: a second 100-foot steel tower was put up at the Peninsula patrol station. The report does not say whether it is this tower.

notes_for_editor: Identity is the main uncertainty. The 1937 report sits under the Peninsula heading but does not name a peninsula station. The July 1938 report describes one moved 100-foot tower and one new 100-foot tower at the Peninsula patrol station; neither is tied to this entry. Possible duplicate: data/research/us-ca-tulelake-nwr.json covers the register record (US 1956, CA 110) at coordinates 41.837882, -121.513237, while this record's brief coordinates are 41.8388, -121.401, roughly 9 km apart by computed distance. The two may be different towers or one tower with a wrong position. Height 30.5 m is 100 feet from the 1937 and 1938 reports; the register's 80-foot figure belongs to the other record. The 1940 memo about a water tower at the peninsula cabin is not about the lookout and is left out. No photos for this entry; the register photos belong to the other record.
